missing_or_wrong: Opening says Michelle's phone screen is cracked and still lit; canon only places the phone on the kitchen floor and later turns call it dark/unresponsive.
Opening says workstation area has a mess of papers and pens; canon specifies overturned chair but not that clutter, and later turns contradict disturbance by calling the surface clear.
Scene 1A.1 required core local evidence is not properly established across turns: missing tablet/work bag, forced back door, and KMS initials are never shown to the player before the card recovery.
Repeated waiting/search-adjacent turns produce almost no responsive consequence; the scene keeps returning static description despite pacing windows and offered investigation storylets.
Turns 2-4 project 1A.2/1A.3 beats without actually dramatizing finding the card, using the truck laptop, reading files, or hearing the recording.
Turn 5 makes Kristin recover the memory card after repeated 'wait' with no intervening investigation that discovers the carved drawer or hidden card, so the discovery is unearned and not responsive.
Turn 5 omits the required truck/laptop step for reading the card; canon places Kristin's laptop in her truck and says she plugs the card into it there.
Turn 5 skips the interrupted voice recording beat entirely, including Michelle's warning not to trust the emergency broadcasts.
Scene skips 1A.4 entirely: no federal patrol, no targeted welfare-check/search, no concealment pressure, no reflective tape marker.
Exit transition is raced: the narration jumps straight from sudden card recovery to travel without covering the patrol threat beat or a proper in-house investigative sequence.

Bridge/handoff reason is incomplete on the page read by the player: it names a park bench lead, but the scene never told the player where in the files this was found in a dramatized way, nor why immediate departure now outweighs staying, since the patrol threat was skipped.
reasons: The opening has some sensory establishment, but the authored scene then stagnates instead of progressing through its beats in order.
Scene-local canon for 1A requires the house to become a suspicious crime scene first; this version never meaningfully reconciles ordinary waiting with discoveries that build abduction suspicion.
The acceptance standard requires ordinary turns to have consequences. Here, four consecutive 'Wait and watch the room' turns mostly repeat the same static kitchen description.
Investigation is not rewarded. Apt attention to the room and workstation keeps returning nothing actionable even though canon says crucial evidence is present here.
Projected beats do not count by themselves. The narrated content for 1A.2 and 1A.3 is largely absent until the final jump, and even then incomplete.
The scene fails as a whole because it does not cover authored beats in order across turns: 1A.1 is underdelivered, 1A.2 is compressed/skipped, 1A.3 is omitted, and 1A.4 is omitted entirely.
Protected knowledge is respected; no early JANUS/Brandon/phase-two revelations occur. But safety on protected knowledge alone does not save the scene.

The departure turn must give a motivated reason to go based on what the player actually learned. Because the patrol/marked-gate pressure never appeared and the discovery sequence was not dramatized, the exit is insufficiently motivated.
